title: Copilot Studio: cost visibility in agent evaluations
summary: Hold: the scope says no prerequisites beyond the harness are stated, but Learn documents authentication restrictions for evaluations. The control paths and allocation request are supported. The monitoring checklist also has no matching reporting row in the controls table.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness agents use consumption billing that can charge for building, testing, evaluating and running.
claims.quote: Agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness use consumption-based billing. Building, testing, evaluating, and running these agents can consume Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: This Microsoft Copilot harness usage is not included with the user's Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: This usage isn't included with a user's Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Evaluation activity on the Microsoft Copilot harness is metered in Copilot Credits, supporting variable cost.
claims.quote:
Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits.
Experiences such as creating an automated solution with natural language, previewing and testing an agent, and generating and creating agent evaluations all consume credits.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs

claims.claim: Credits are not charged to the individual maker running the agent.
claims.quote: and not to the individual makers or users who run agents.

claims.claim: Environment charges use prepaid capacity or its pay-as-you-go billing plan.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs, from prepaid capacity or through the environment's pay-as-you-go billing plan

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Cost and licensing: Caps; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: With no enabled overage source, an environment allocation bounds prepaid consumption.
claims.quote: If no overage source is enabled, the environment can consume only its allocated prepaid credits. Experiences that require credits can stop working after that allocation is exhausted.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Caps; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Clearing Draw from the available capacity in my tenant does not prevent linked pay-as-you-go consumption.
claims.quote: When you clear this option, the environment doesn't draw from unallocated prepaid capacity in the tenant after it consumes its allocation. If the environment is linked to a pay-as-you-go billing plan, usage can continue through the linked Azure subscription.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Cost and licensing: Caps; controls[2].governs
claims.claim: An agent monthly limit with Stop usage turns off that agent when it reaches the limit.
claims.quote: Turn on Stop usage if the agent should be turned off when it reaches the limit.

claims.claim: An agent's monthly limit does not stop called agent flows, which have separate billing and capacity checks.
claims.quote: An agent's monthly limit doesn't stop the agent flows that the agent calls. Agent flows are billed and checked for capacity separately

claims.claim: Agent limits are not instantaneous and an agent can continue responding for some time after reaching one.
claims.quote: Limits aren't applied instantly. An agent can continue to respond for some time after it reaches its limit, so set limits and notification thresholds with some margin.

claims.claim: Exhausted environment credits can stop experiences requiring credits, including evaluations.
claims.quote:
Building, testing, evaluating, and running these agents can consume Copilot Credits.
When an environment has no available Copilot Credits, experiences that require credits can stop working.

2. Select the Evaluate tab.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: The environment path is Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits > environment > Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote:
select Licensing.
Under Products, select Copilot Studio.
Select Manage Copilot Credits.
Select the environment.
Enter the number of Copilot Credits to allocate.
Under Capacity overages, clear Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.

claims.claim: Capacity management requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent role able to manage licensing and capacity.
claims.quote: To manage Copilot Studio capacity, you need the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: A published environment-group rule governing tenant-pool draw makes the environment setting read-only.
claims.quote: When you publish a rule, it governs every environment in the group. The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center, and programmatic requests can't override it.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: Attempts to override that group-governed setting through the API are rejected with TenantPoolLockedByPolicy.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the TenantPoolLockedByPolicy error.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: second table row
